correctness.rationale: Split diameter-three anticode by inversion parity; each slice has diameter <=2. Normalize a slice member to identity: other members correspond to two-inversion graph edges. Pairwise intersecting edges form a star or triangle; maximum degree n-2, and equality for n>=5 yields a full star (no triangles when n=5). This identifies each full parity slice as unique N(a). For equality total 2(n-1), both slices are such neighborhoods, and if centers are not adjacent a large-inversion neighbor violates cross distance <=3. Adjacent center double balls attain bound, center edge unique; counting edges yields n!(n-1)/2 and orbit positions i~n-i. Independent enumeration verified two-inversion patterns for n5/6/7 and all 240/1800 double balls with distinct center edges for n5/6; unrestricted proof does not rely on finite tests.
